FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
The Basic Speed Rule sets no exact cap but limits speed to what stays safe for current conditions with stopping short of anyone, so a posted sixty-five can still run too fast on a rainy foggy night two-lane [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Speed must stay careful and prudent with skill and judgment plus reasonable and proper neither too fast nor too slow for traffic amount and pace, pedestrian presence especially schoolchildren, road surface, width, and structure, visibility, weather and air, and your own ability [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Never crawl so slowly as to block, hinder, or interfere with normal-speed traffic, and always fit speed to conditions so you halt within clear distance ahead, since rear-ending a suddenly stopped leader breaks the rule or proves tailgating even under the posted cap [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
The law bars driving faster than careful and prudent, faster or slower than reasonable and proper for traffic, surface, width, and all existing conditions, and faster than stopping within assured clear distance allows [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Speeding convictions can draw fines up to six hundred fifty-four dollars plus thirty days in jail, and fines double in school and construction zones where workers or equipment stand [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A02
Unless otherwise posted in normal conditions the state caps run seventy-five on controlled-access highways, eighty on turnpikes, sixty-five on undivided state highways, fifty-five on county roads, thirty-five in state parks and wildlife refuges, and twenty-five in properly marked rural school zones [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A02
Cities and towns set their own changing zone caps, so drivers watch and obey every posted business, residential, and school-zone limit with special care [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
Turns should run ten miles per hour or less [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A02
Night shrinks clear sight on dim highways and country roads where dark animals, objects, walkers, and riders hide, so slow for road and weather, never outdrive your lights, fit speed to lamp power and brake response, and stay able to halt for anything appearing ahead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
Shun sunglasses and colored lenses at night and on dark days, since headlight, billboard, and streetlight glare already slows eye adjustment and tinted lenses slow it further while cutting vision [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
Road rage spans tailgating, cutoffs, careless changes, speeding, and red-running up through obscene gestures, verbal assault, intentional ramming, and weapon threats, and drivers should avoid offending or engaging others, master their anger, and when targeted flee to a peopled police, fire, or gas station, call nine-one-one if needed, and never drive home [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0041]
